content.intro: This lesson focuses on your first practical yaml configuration and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: Your First Practical YAML Configuration matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: YAML uses indentation to express hierarchy. Mappings associate keys with values, sequences preserve order, and scalars represent leaf values. Consistent spaces and an appropriate editor prevent common structure errors.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover

Comparing the YAML structure with a JSON equivalent.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Your First Practical YAML Configuration
content_blocks.code:
app:
  name: Field Notes
  port: 8080
  features:
    search: true
    export: false
content_blocks.expected_output: This configuration uses nested mappings and explicit scalar types; verify the expected types in the application that consumes it.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as example.yaml and validate it with the exact parser/linter used by the target application. For Python experiments, use an isolated environment and safe loading for untrusted content. Do not assume every parser resolves ambiguous scalars identically.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the starting fixture before each test. Change one field, indentation level, parser option, or schema constraint at a time, then compare the result with the prediction.
content_blocks.limitations: This snippet is a reference/example, not evidence that the CodeLeaf browser executes JSON/YAML parsing, shell commands, or Python. Validate locally with a named parser or tool before relying on it.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Indentation and scalar interpretation are part of the data model. Quote ambiguous strings, use consistent spaces, and test with the parser/schema that the target application actually uses. Confirm implementation-specific behavior against the target parser, tool version, and standards documentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
